summary: Iteration 3: tested Calibration Sessions and Agent Self-Review through the API and the UI, plus regression. Backend: new suite tests/test_iter3_calibration_selfreview.py passed 15/15. It covers: agents get 403; create validation (agent or unknown participant gives 400, empty list gives 422, missing interaction gives 404); the blind view for a participant who has not submitted (scores [], revealed false, spread {}); a missing criterion gives 400; a score over 100 gives 422; a non-participant gets 403; re-submitting replaces your own entry; the weighted overall and the per-criterion spread including the AI score; only the owner can close (others 403); closing with apply_to_interaction updates overall_score and criteria_results, keeps original_score and sets auto_failed false; scoring or closing a closed session gives 409; a non-participant gets 404 on GET and cannot see the session in the list; self-review sorts notes, others get 404, an unscored interaction gives 400, and bad notes give 422. The old regression suites (test_cadence_api + test_iter2_features) passed 33, with 3 skipped because /tmp/call.mp3 is missing. UI checked with admin, a temporary QA auditor and the agent: the Calibration nav item is visible to staff and hidden from the agent (the agent sees the 'for team leads' message). 'Start calibration session' on the interaction page opens the dialog with the interaction already selected and the current user ticked. Creating a session goes to the detail page. The QA auditor sees calibration-locked before submitting; after submitting, the comparison table shows AI + Asha Admin + TEST_Quinn columns with spread chips. The owner's 'Agree the standard' form was prefilled with the average (70/60/70/60). With the apply switch turned off, close shows calibration-agreed-overall 66.7 and the guidance note, and sample-3 stayed at 85. Self-review as the agent on 68b74230: the audio plays; 'Add at time' captured 0:05 and Enter also adds a note; notes are sorted; remove works; clicking a timestamp seeks; reflection save persists after reload. The admin sees a read-only view (no inputs) where timestamps still seek. The interactions list shows interaction-self-reviewed-68b74230. Creating coaching from it prefills the notes with the AI summary, "Agent's self-review: ..." and '• 0:12 — should have paused here'. Dashboard, interactions, disputes, coaching, settings (digest preview) and transcript-segment seek still work, with no page errors. One logic issue found: the session owner or an admin who is a participant sees everyone else's scores before submitting their own, so scoring is not blind for them.

critical.issue: Blind scoring can be bypassed. reveal = closed OR submitted OR user is the creator OR role is admin. So the session owner (e.g. the team lead who created it) and any admin who is also a participant see the other scores, the spread and the comparison table before submitting their own. Reproduced: TL creates a session with TL + QA, QA submits, and TL's GET returns revealed=true, submitted=false, scores=[QA entry]. The UI says 'Other reviewers' scores unlock once you submit', but for admin and owner the comparison is already shown. Suggested fix: if the user is a participant and has not submitted (and the session is open), hide the scores even when they are the owner or an admin. Only reveal early to an owner or admin who is not a participant.

minor.issue: Binary criteria (type 'binary', '0 = fail, 100 = pass') accept any value from 0 to 100, e.g. 70. When applied, passed is set from score >= 60 and the agreed binary result can be 70. Consider allowing only 0 or 100 for binary criteria.

auto_failed is always set to false, even when the group gives an auto_fail criterion 0. The applied interaction then shows a passing score for a call that should auto-fail. Consider auto_failed = any(c.auto_fail and score < 60).

Not atomic. The session is set to closed before the interaction is loaded, so if the interaction was deleted it returns 404 but the session stays closed with applied=true. The close is also a find-then-update with no status filter, so two closes at the same time can both succeed. Use update_one({'id':cid,'status':'open'}) and check modified_count.

Re-submit is a $pull followed by a separate $push, with no status filter. Two submits at the same time from the same user can leave duplicate entries, and a score can land just after the session closes. Consider a single update with a status:'open' filter.
After a calibration is applied, rescore overwrites the agreed score, unsets original_score and leaves calibrated_by stale. Consider blocking or warning for calibrated interactions.

ui_bugs.issue: For an admin or owner participant the 'Score this call blind' form is shown next to the visible comparison table (follows from the backend reveal logic above)

issues: Spread chips are labelled '±40' but the value is the full range (max-min), not ± half. Use 'Δ40' or 'range 40'.
For chat/email interactions the left card header still says 'Call recording · No recording stored'; show only the transcript or call it 'Conversation'.
The Due and Scheduled-for fields use the browser's native date pickers instead of the shadcn Calendar/Popover.
Unknown routes (e.g. /digest) show a blank page with no 'not found' message.

action_items: Make calibration blind for every participant who has not submitted, including the owner and admins (backend _cal_view + CalibrationDetail)
Allow only 0 or 100 for binary criteria in calibration score/close
When applying the agreed score, set auto_failed from the agreed auto_fail criteria instead of always false
Make close and score atomic with a status:'open' filter; load and check the interaction before marking the session closed
Optional: fix the spread label (±), the 'Call recording' header for non-voice interactions, add a 404 route, and use the shadcn date picker
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 1039 lines (>700). Move calibration, self-review and disputes into their own router modules.
_cal_view reveal condition: creator/admin bypass defeats blind calibration (see the critical issue)
close_calibration: non-atomic status transition, and the interaction update happens after the session is closed
The participant_names snapshot is taken at creation; renamed users show their old names (acceptable, but note it)

success_rate.backend: 100% (15/15 new + 33/33 regression, 3 skipped for missing /tmp/call.mp3); 1 blind-reveal logic issue found with a separate repro
success_rate.frontend: 95% (all flows work; blind view leaks for admin/owner participants)
